raw: Act 2, Scene 1 — An open place adjoining Capulet’s Garden

speaker: CHORUS
raw:
Now old desire doth in his deathbed lie,
And young affection gapes to be his heir;
That fair for which love groan’d for and would die,
With tender Juliet match’d, is now not fair.
Now Romeo is belov’d, and loves again,
Alike bewitched by the charm of looks;
But to his foe suppos’d he must complain,
And she steal love’s sweet bait from fearful hooks:
Being held a foe, he may not have access
To breathe such vows as lovers use to swear;
And she as much in love, her means much less
To meet her new beloved anywhere.
But passion lends them power, time means, to meet,
Tempering extremities with extreme sweet.

sentences.en: Now old desire lies in its deathbed.
Young affection is ready to take its place.
The beauty Romeo once longed for and would die for now seems plain next to tender Juliet.
Now Romeo is loved, and he loves again.
Both are enchanted by each other's looks.
But he must tell his love to a girl from his enemy's family.
And she must take love's sweet bait from a dangerous hook.
Because he is seen as an enemy, he cannot visit her.
He cannot say the vows that lovers usually swear.
She is just as much in love.
But she has even fewer ways to meet her new love.
But passion gives them power, and time gives them chances to meet.
It mixes extreme danger with extreme sweetness.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Can I go forward when my heart is here?
Turn back, dull earth, and find thy centre out.

sentences.en: Can I move forward when my heart is here?
Turn back, dull body, and find your heart's center.

raw: He climbs the wall and leaps down within it.

sentences.en: Romeo climbs the wall and jumps down inside it.
Romeo!
My cousin Romeo!
Romeo!

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
He is wise,
And on my life hath stol’n him home to bed.

sentences.en: He is wise.
And I swear on my life that he has gone home to bed.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
He ran this way, and leap’d this orchard wall:
Call, good Mercutio.

sentences.en: He ran this way.
He jumped over this orchard wall.
Call out, good Mercutio.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Nay, I’ll conjure too.
Romeo! Humours! Madman! Passion! Lover!
Appear thou in the likeness of a sigh,
Speak but one rhyme, and I am satisfied;
Cry but ‘Ah me!’ Pronounce but Love and dove;
Speak to my gossip Venus one fair word,
One nickname for her purblind son and heir,
Young Abraham Cupid, he that shot so trim
When King Cophetua lov’d the beggar-maid.
He heareth not, he stirreth not, he moveth not;
The ape is dead, and I must conjure him.
I conjure thee by Rosaline’s bright eyes,
By her high forehead and her scarlet lip,
By her fine foot, straight leg, and quivering thigh,
And the demesnes that there adjacent lie,
That in thy likeness thou appear to us.

sentences.en: No, I will call him up like a magician too.
Romeo! Moods! Madman! Passion! Lover!
Appear in the form of a sigh.
Speak just one rhyme and I will be satisfied.
Cry out 'Ah me!'
Say only Love and dove.
Tell my friend Venus one fair word.
Give one nickname to her blind son and heir.
Young Abraham Cupid shot so well when King Cophetua loved the beggar-maid.
He does not hear.
He does not move.
He does not stir.
The monkey is playing dead, and I must summon him.
I summon you by Rosaline's bright eyes.
By her high forehead and her red lip.
By her fine foot, straight leg, and shaking thigh.
And by the parts that lie near them.
Appear to us in your likeness.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: An if he hear thee, thou wilt anger him.

sentences.en: If he hears you, you will make him angry.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
This cannot anger him. ’Twould anger him
To raise a spirit in his mistress’ circle,
Of some strange nature, letting it there stand
Till she had laid it, and conjur’d it down;
That were some spite. My invocation
Is fair and honest, and, in his mistress’ name,
I conjure only but to raise up him.

sentences.en: This cannot make him angry.
It would only anger him if I caused a spirit of a strange nature to appear in his mistress's circle.
That spirit would stay there until she had laid it and sent it away.
That would be mean.
My request is fair and honest.
I am using her name only to make him appear.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Come, he hath hid himself among these trees
To be consorted with the humorous night.
Blind is his love, and best befits the dark.

sentences.en: Come, he has hidden himself among these trees.
He wants to be with the moody night.
His love is blind.
It is best for his love to stay in the dark.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
If love be blind, love cannot hit the mark.
Now will he sit under a medlar tree,
And wish his mistress were that kind of fruit
As maids call medlars when they laugh alone.
O Romeo, that she were, O that she were
An open-arse and thou a poperin pear!
Romeo, good night. I’ll to my truckle-bed.
This field-bed is too cold for me to sleep.
Come, shall we go?

sentences.en: If love is blind, love cannot hit the mark.
Now he will sit under a medlar tree.
He will wish his girl were a medlar.
Girls laugh that the medlar looks like a bottom.
Oh Romeo, I wish she were that bottom-shaped fruit, and you a long, pointed pear!
Romeo, good night.
I will go to my own bed.
This field-bed is too cold for me to sleep.
Come, shall we go?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Go then; for ’tis in vain
To seek him here that means not to be found.

sentences.en: Go then.
It is useless to look for him here.
He does not want to be found.
